name: straight_cut_6sq
source: racing_game-owned straight-cut 6-speed sequential dog gearbox for racing, an invented design, NOT a specific gearbox [AS]. Ratios 2.95 / 2.12 / 1.62 / 1.31 / 1.03 / 0.76, steps 1.39 / 1.31 / 1.24 / 1.27 / 1.36 (under the 1.62 limit that car_hyper_n2o's Sport-mode auto-shift points, up 8100 / down 5000 rpm, allow without hunting). Straight-cut (spur) gears have no axial sliding component, so mesh efficiency is higher than a helical box: 0.985 per gear against 0.97-0.98 [AS, rationale only: a spur mesh loses power to rolling friction alone, a helical one adds axial sliding friction; the figure is assumed, not cited]. Dog engagement, no cone synchros, short shift times: sequential drum, neutral dwell 0.025 s, dog release 150 N*m, grind after 0.20 s, abort 0.60 s [AS]. MODEL NOTE: physics_sim only matches the input shaft speed through a synchro capacity (zero capacity grinds on every auto-shift), so the capacity here (90 N*m, 6 gears and reverse) is the model's stand-in for the ECU-assisted dog speed match (torque cut and blip), together with a wide dog mismatch window (25 rad/s at the input shaft, about 240 rpm, chamfered dog teeth) [AS]; the catalogue lists the box as synchro 'dog'. Light shafts (input 0.008, output 0.012 kg*m2). Torque rating 1800 N*m (enough for the hypercar) is kept in data/gearboxes/gearbox_catalog.json.
